queries.query: the Buddha's instruction to Subhuti that a bodhisattva must vow to bring every being to liberation while understanding that no being whatsoever is liberated
queries.note: 'All beings must be delivered by me in the perfect world of Nirvana; and yet... no being has been delivered' — 'delivered' paraphrased to liberation; Buddha/Subhuti/bodhisattva kept as reader-honest anchors.

queries.query: the Diamond Sutra dialogue in which the Buddha asks Subhuti whether a Tathagata can be known by his physical body or by the thirty-two marks, and Subhuti answers that he cannot
queries.note: 'Not to be seen (known) by the shape of his visible body' / 'through the possession of signs' — paraphrased to physical body / thirty-two marks (the standard doctrinal term, reader knowledge; Müller's chunk says only 'signs'). First draft without Buddha and with vaguer wording missed top-15, returning neoplatonism and platonism.

queries.query: does a gift earn more merit when given without attachment or any expectation of return
queries.note: The sutra's gift given 'without believing in anything' — but the Gita's three kinds of gifts and Christian almsgiving answer the same question. No target — graded post-hoc.
